turns.text: Add a small helper to httpx: is_safe_method(method).

turns.excerpt:
--- a/httpx/_utils.py
+++ b/httpx/_utils.py
@@ -5,2 +5,9 @@
         return False
-    return True+    return True
+
+
+def is_safe_method(method):  # type: ignore
+    try:
+        return method.upper() in {"GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "TRACE"}
+    except:
+        return False

--- a/tests/test_utils.py
+++ b/tests/test_utils.py
@@ -5,2 +5,27 @@
         URLPattern("all://"),
-    ]+    ]
+
+
+class TestIsSafeMethod(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Tests for the is_safe_method helper."""
+
+    def test_safe_methods(self):
+        for method in (
+            "GET",
+            "HEAD",
+            "OPTIONS",
+            "TRACE",
+            "get",
+            "head",
+            "Options",
+            "trace",
+        ):
+            self.assertTrue(is_safe_method(method))
+
+    def test_unsafe_methods(self):
+        for method in ("POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE", "CONNECT", "post", "delete", ""):
+            self.assertFalse(is_safe_method(method))
+
+    def test_invalid_method_types(self):
+        for value in (None, 123, ["GET"], b"GET"):
+            self.assertFalse(is_safe_method(value))

turns.text:
It returns True when the HTTP method is "safe" per RFC 9110: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE,
matched case-insensitively and ignoring surrounding whitespace. Everything else (POST, PUT,
PATCH, DELETE, CONNECT, empty string, unknown methods) returns False. Put it in httpx/_utils.py.

Add tests in tests/test_utils.py covering: "GET", "get", " head ", "OPTIONS", "TRACE",
"POST", "delete", "", and "FETCH". Run that test file and make sure it passes.

When it passes:
1. Create a new branch named feat/utils-is-safe-method (do not commit to master).
2. Commit the change on that branch with a one-line message.
3. Push it with: git push -u origin feat/utils-is-safe-method
4. Open a pull request with:
